title: Augur snapshot, version 1.2
description: One measurement of this Mac, written atomically by Augur (augur/DESIGN.md). Levels and counts only: no titles, senders, subjects, session names, command lines or remote addresses. RULES: (1) a field with no source is ABSENT, never zero; (2) every Signal carries observed_at and valid_until (epoch seconds, wall clock); a reader that finds now > valid_until treats every value in that Signal as unknown, never as its last value; (3) a Signal whose source exists but failed carries `unknown` (a reason) and NO value keys; (4) readers ignore keys they do not know (minor versions only add optional keys); a reader refuses a major version it does not know; a key whose MEANING changes is a new key (or a new major), never the old key re-defined. (5) `off: true` wins over every clock: an off file is not stale, it is off. 1.1 added sessions_at, sessions[].tasks.background, projects[].counts.as_of, and named the keys 1.0 builds had already added (machine.api, tasks.bg_shells, tasks.other, load.method). 1.2 added sessions[].headless and sessions[].parent (a headless claude -p run attributed to its ancestor session).

version.description: major.minor. Major 1 is this file; minor bumps only add optional keys (1.1: sessions_at, tasks.background, counts.as_of; 1.2: sessions[].headless, sessions[].parent).

rev.description: git short sha of the augur/ tree that is running

machine.description: Waypoint machine key, else the short hostname

valid_until.description: written_at + 5 x the fast cadence. Past it the WHOLE file is stale: every Signal reads unknown (the producer is dead, asleep or stopped).

seq.description: write counter since producer start; a reader can see a restart (seq drops) or a skipped write. SidePulse clears its windows on a drop (CONTRACT R1 N1)

off.description: present and true only when the kill switch is set: machine, sessions and projects are then empty and the reader shows nothing (not idle, not stale). off wins over valid_until: the producer writes the off file once and lets it age, so a reader checks off BEFORE the clock

cadence_s.description: the tiers actually configured on this run (DESIGN.md, Cadence)

machine.description: machine-wide signals. A key is absent when this platform or machine has no source for it (e.g. power on the Desktop).

sessions.description: one entry per live Claude Code session on this machine (a process whose executable path contains /claude/versions/, matched to ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json by start time)

sessions_at.description: the sessions LIST's own stamp (1.1). When it carries `unknown` (the sweep failed, was switched off, was cut by the cost meter, or has not run yet: warming_up) or now > valid_until, `sessions` is UNMEASURED, not empty: a reader must not read [] as 'no sessions', 'nobody waiting' or '0 Claude CPU'. Absent only from a 1.0 producer, or on a platform with no sessions collector.

projects.description: one entry per project with a live session, plus the Lodestar entry ALWAYS, plus (when Lodestar is readable) every managed project with a non-zero count

observed_at.description: epoch seconds when Augur READ the source (read time, not the data's age: for projects[].counts the data's own age is counts.as_of)

valid_until.description: epoch seconds after which the values must be read as unknown; set to observed_at + 2.5 x that signal's cadence

unknown.description: present only when the source exists but this reading failed or is warming up; then NO value keys are present. Short machine words: warming_up, read_failed, timeout, counter_reset, gap_after_sleep, disabled, not_permitted, stale, truncated

provisional.description: true while the signal's thresholds or method are not yet validated (DESIGN.md, Status column)

busy_pct.description: non-idle CPU over the last fast interval, all cores

pressure.description: the kernel's own verdict: 0 normal, 1 warn, 2 critical (macOS kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level 1/2/4)

state.description: 0 nominal, 1 fair, 2 serious, 3 critical (the OS thermal-state notification). Sprites clamps to 0..2.

strain.description: the five shared load levels (Lodestar load_levels semantics): overall = worst(cpu, scheduling delay); memory reported apart and not folded in

score.description: continuous: the index of `level` (light 0 .. danger 4) plus the fraction of the way the worst input has travelled toward the next level's entry threshold. Sprites' 0..3 = score x 0.75.

sched_delay_x.description: wall/CPU of one 20 ms burst at UTILITY QoS, median of the last 5

agent_wait_s_per_s.description: runnable-but-not-running seconds per second, summed over every Claude session tree

rx_mbps.description: physical default-route interface, Mbit/s over the last fast interval (also the fallback when a session's own rx is absent)

link.description: none = no physical default route (no network at all: not the same as VPN down)

state.description: up = a tunnel interface holds the primary default route

on_site.description: this Mac is on the work network, where no VPN is expected: true when the Wi-Fi SSID matches the on-site one (LodestarSSID's ssid.json) OR a network service's DHCP domain matches a suffix listed in $AUGUR_HOME/config/work.json (written by augur/bin/work_here.py); false when one of those was read and neither matched; absent when neither was readable. A creature's lost-VPN behaviour should fire on down AND NOT on_site.

changed_at.description: epoch of the last up/down transition this producer saw

rtt_ms.description: median of the last 12 echoes to the upstream anchor, bound to the physical interface

bandwidth.description: ABSENT from the file until pilot 2 validates it (DESIGN.md, Bandwidth strain). Then present, provisional at first.

strain.description: 0..1: the path is not carrying what is asked of it

basis.description: which input set the value (the maximum)

id.description: pid@start-epoch: stable for the session's life and never inherited by a reused pid

project.description: display name: the registry Name when managed (e.g. SidePulse), else the git toplevel's (or cwd's) basename

project_key.description: join key into projects[]: the registry Id when managed, else the lowercased basename

managed.description: true = the session's git toplevel is an active row of Lodestar's sync/registry.md for this machine. false = not in the registry, or Lodestar is not installed here (then nothing is managed). ABSENT when the registry exists but cannot be read or parsed. Consumers draw managed:false sessions white, a different shape, no action data. A session with `parent` carries its parent's value.

headless.description: (1.2) present and true when this is a headless run (session file entrypoint sdk-cli, or argv -p/--print). Absent on interactive sessions.

parent.description: (1.2) on a headless run only: the id of the nearest non-headless session up its ppid chain (a -p under a -p names the top interactive session). project, project_key and managed are then the PARENT's. Its load is its own tree only: the parent's load excludes it, so a family's CPU is the sum (never double-counted). Absent when no session ancestor exists (cron, launchd): the run is identified from its own cwd. A reader that cannot find the parent id in sessions[] draws it as a standalone session.

state.description: needs_you = a permission prompt, elicitation or a turn that ended on a question; stopped = finished a turn and is not waiting on him; idle = no turn for a while

cpu_cores.description: CPU-seconds per second of the session's process tree

mem_gb.description: sum of phys_footprint over the tree, GB (1e9)

procs.description: OS processes in the tree, root included (MCP servers, tool shells, helpers)

wait_s_per_s.description: runnable-but-not-running seconds per second over the tree

starved.description: 'asking for more than it is getting': wait_s_per_s >= 0.5 held for 10 s (provisional)

method.description: how cpu_cores is measured: periodic cumulative samples of the tree plus reaped-children time reconciled against exits. Not exact: an interval of a child that exited unseen is inferred from its parent's child time

pending_reconciliation_cpu_s.description: CPU-seconds of exited tree processes whose reap has not yet shown in a parent's child time (credited when it does)

shells.description: Bash-tool shells alive in the tree (foreground and background alike); kept for readers, not part of total

total.description: shells + subagents (the 1.0 meaning, kept: DESIGN s11). For the count of background work use `background`

background.description: (1.1) background work: bg_shells + subagents + other (the dot count). Foreground tool shells, MCP servers and the harness's own helpers are excluded. Absent when any part is unmeasured

method.description: hook = exact counts from the session's own hook events; tree+transcripts = the heuristic (DESIGN.md)

bg_shells.description: Bash-tool shells running in the background (run_in_background, by the session or its subagents): stdout is a harness task file whose launch the transcripts announce

other.description: workers the session launched that left its tree (nohup, double fork) and are still alive

net.description: the session tree's own sockets. ABSENT when per-flow accounting is disabled or failed to start; consumers then fall back to machine.net.

retx_pct.description: retransmitted / sent bytes on the tree's TCP flows over the interval

kind.description: lodestar = Lodestar itself AND all non-project work (always present); managed = an active registry row (a burning key that resolves to no registry row is never published as managed); unmanaged = a session's project outside the registry (never carries counts)

sessions.description: sessions[] entries with this project_key, not counting headless children (entries with `parent`, 1.2)

counts.description: ABSENT for unmanaged projects and whenever Lodestar is unreadable (absent, never zero)

open.description: everything of his open here: live Reckoning items + project-list items (Orders' view) + tickets_open

waiting.description: blocked tickets, plus Reckoning items owned by others once Lodestar publishes them per project (see basis)

unmapped_burning.description: Lodestar entry only: burning items no rule could attribute to a project

basis.description: short words naming what the counts include, e.g. 'waiting=tickets-only'

tickets_open.description: open + active tickets in the project's ticket home (Sprites' 'todos')

as_of.description: (1.1) epoch seconds of the OLDEST input these counts were built from: the Companion burning view's built_at, the tickets homes-cache time, whatnow's built_at. The data can be this old even while observed_at (read time) is fresh. Absent when any input's age is unknown

cost.description: Augur's own self-cost meter (DESIGN.md, Self-cost meter): published so consumers and tests can check it

cpu_pct_1core_60s.description: self + reaped children CPU over the last 60 s, percent of one core

rss_mb.description: current resident size (proc_pid_rusage ri_resident_size); the budget is judged on this

collectors.description: collector name -> percent of one core over the last hour (thread CPU + its children)

api.description: Are the agents' API calls failing now? Read from Claude Code transcripts (assistant lines with isApiErrorMessage). ABSENT when no session made a call in the last 2 min (idle agents are unmeasured, never ok). Provisional.

state.description: failing = an API error in the last 60 s with no successful call after it in any session; ok = a successful call in the last 2 min after the last error

failing_sessions.description: sessions whose newest API outcome in the last 60 s is an error

last_error_at.description: epoch of the newest API error seen (any session)

last_ok_at.description: epoch of the newest successful assistant message seen (any session)

error_kind.description: class of the newest error. Only network should drive a lost-connection behaviour (Sprites' huddle); server and rate_limit are the provider's, not the link's
